sentences.text:
* * 
 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271, alleging that on 12.01.2024 at about 05.40 a.m., when riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-ER- 8719 on the Service road, Electronic city Metro station,
driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to rear part of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-ER-8719, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2.

Petitioner took treatment at Kauvery Hospital, Bengaluru and St.John's Medical college hospital,
Bengaluru.
3. Regarding the accident Electronic City police registered a case in crime No.11/2024.
4. As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.17,000/- p.m. by doing contract work in private companies.

5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 owner of the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 appeared through his advocate, however, did not file written statement, on 25.04.2024 produced copy of the policy, RC pertaining to Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AD-3271 and Driving Licence of Prashanth, S/o.Shekar Gowda at Exs.R.1 to R.3.
6.

In response to the notice, respondent No.2 Insurance Company appeared through his advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 13.11.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 12.01.2024 at about 05.40 a.m., on the service road, near Metro Station, Electronic city, Bengaluru, in view of the negligent use of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AD-3271, Car dashed to the rear side of the Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-ER-8719, thereby accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner, rider of the Motorcycle?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80323028/
2 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 30.12.2024, 13.01.2025, 24.02.2025 petitioner deposed as P.W.1 and produced 15 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.15.

On 04.04.2025 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.Ramachandra as P.W.2 and get produced 2 documents at Exs.P.16 and 17.
9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of the material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.3,54,379/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- In the evidence petitioner/P.W.1 stated that on 12.01.2024 at 05.40 a.m. when riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-ER-8719 on the Service road, Electronic city Metro station, driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to rear part of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-ER- 8719, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
12. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
13. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 stated that when he was riding Motorcycle from Anekal towards Electronic City under Electronic City Metro station met with an accident.
Petitioner stated that when he was riding Motorcycle on the service road, car which came from back side dashed to the Motorcycle.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that at early morning rode the Motorcycle negligently and dashed the same to the front right part of the car.
14. In the evidence of P.W.2 - Dr.Ramachandra stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

15. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.11/2024 registered by Electronic City police on 13.01.2024 against Prashanth, the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint/statement of the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Wound Certificate, in which reason for the injuries are noted as alleged history of RTA on 12.01.2024 at 5.30 a.m. at Electronic City.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of Motor Vehicles Accident Report.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet filed by Electronic City police in Cr.No.11/2024 against Prashanth, S/o.Shekar Gowda, driver of Car bearing No.No.KA-04-AD-3271 for having committed offence punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80323028/
3 IPC.
16.

entities.text: Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

17. Hence, I have concluded that on 12.01.2024 at about 05.40 a.m. when petitioner was riding Motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-ER-8719 on the Service road, Electronic city Metro station,
Prashanth, S/o.Shaker Gowda, negligently drove the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271, dashed the same to rear part of Motorcycle bearing No.KA- 05-ER-8719, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

18. Issue No.2: In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident, he has suffered LS Spine wedge compression, fracture of L2 Vertebra body a linear T1 Hypo T2/stir Hyper intensity was noted involving the right lateral aspect of the superior portion of the 12 Vertebral body with mild reduction in the vertebral body height, CT Correlation wedge compression fracture involving the 12 vertebral body with a small posteriorly displaced fracture fragment causing mild compression of the anterior,
took treatment at Kauvery hospital and St.John's Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru, by spending Rs.2,50,000/-.
Petitioner stated that, as on the date of accident, being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.17,000/- p.m. by working on contract basis in private companies.
19. In the written statement, respondent No.2 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

20. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated that immediately after the accident, Toll ambulance vehicle persons shifted him to Kauvery Hospital, then shifted to ESI Hospital, situated at Indira Nagar, then shifted to St.John's medical college Hospital, Koramangala.
Petitioner stated that he has been treated conservatively.
Petitioner stated that, he is working as a Security Guard under a contractor at Infosys, Electronic city and in view of his absence, Infosys terminated his employment.

21. During evidence, P.W.1 shown his identity card issued by Dabarman Security Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
in the Mobile.

During cross-examination, P.W.1 shown salary slip for the month of December 2024,
in which Rs.17,996/- is shown as basic, Rs.374/- is shown as HRA, Rs.300/- is shown as washing allowance, Rs.1,864/- is shown as OT (total amount of salary is noted as Rs.20,504/-).
In the evidence petitioner stated that since from the date of accident, he is wearing belt to the waist.
In the evidence P.W.1 admitted non-production of documents regarding his occupation and income.

22. In the evidence affidavit P.W.2-Dr.Ramachandra stated that on 20.01.2025 when clinically examined the petitioner, noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent residual physical disability of about 38.48% of Vertebral column, which is about 14.24% to whole body.

In the evidence P.W.2 produced OPD card dated 20.01.2025 and and 4 X-rays at Exs.P.16 and 17.
23.
In the cross-examination P.W.2 stated that he has not treated the petitioner, on the basis of Discharge Summary, Wound Certificate and stand report, estimated physical disability of the petitioner.
P.W.2 submitted ignorance about avocation of the petitioner.

Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80323028/
4 24.

entities.text: Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wound Certificate, Discharge Summaries, X-rays and other medical documents shows that in the accident petitioner suffered Wedge compression fracture of L2, took treatment at Kauvery hospital and St.John's Medical College Hospital from 12.01.2024 to 18.01.2024, then took follow up treatment.
25. In the copy of Driving Licence, Aadhar Card and AN Card marked at Ex.P.9 to 11, date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 25.04.1989.
Medical bills shows that petitioner spent Rs.27,379/- for treatment.
26. As referred above, during cross-examination, as per the salary slip shown by P.W.1, during December 2024, P.W.1/petitioner earned Rs.17,996/- p.m. as basic.
In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding quantum of his income during January 2024.
27. In this case, there are no evidence to show either loss of income or decrease in the income of petitioner subsequent to treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of P.W.2-Dr.Ramachandra is insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income (functional disability).
28.

Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, I award compensation under the following heads:
Sl
. No .
Heads of Compensation Amount (Rs.)

1) Pain and agony 1,00,000.00 2) Treatment charges 27,379.00 3) Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000.00 attendant charges 4) Loss of income during treatment 1,32,000.00 period (Rs.16,500/- x 8)
5) Loss of amenities and future 80,000.00 unhappiness:
Total: 3,54,379.00 29.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.3,54,379/-
with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.
33. Issue No.3:

Even though in the written statement respondent No.2 - Insurance Company denied the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 contested the case (cross examined P.W.1 and 2) as if insurer of the car.

Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80323028/
5 34.

entities.text: Nagoor Basha K vs Mukunda B G
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.1 shows that as on the date of incident, Car had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
Copy of the Driving License marked at Ex.R.3 shows that as on the date of incident, Prashanth against whom police have filed charge sheet, had license to drive light motor vehicle (Car).

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer Issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.3,54,379/- (Rupees Three lakhs Fifty four thousand Three hundred and Seventy nine only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-04-AD-3271 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 6th day of May, 2025.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
